intended_object: The canonical topological group isomorphism between the pro-p group ⟨x₁, x₂ | [x₁, x₂]⟩ (the one-relator pro-p group whose relator is the commutator of the two generators) and ℤ_p × ℤ_p. It sends xᵢ to the coordinate vector eᵢ, so it is induced by the exponent-sum map. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is built in two steps:

1. **Same closed normal subgroup.** `topologicalClosure_normalClosure_demushkinWordNeTwo_zero_two` shows that the closed normal closure of the relator `demushkinWordNeTwo 0 2` equals the kernel of the exponent-sum map `freeProP p (Fin 2) → Multiplicative (Fin 2 → ℤ_[p])`. The kernel is closed and normal, so it also equals the closed normal closure of itself. `congrOfClosureEq` therefore identifies the presented group with the quotient by that kernel.
2. **First isomorphism theorem.** Because the exponent-sum map is surjective, `presentedProP.equivOfSurjective` identifies that quotient with ℤ_p × ℤ_p. The result is a topological isomorphism.

The library proves `presentedProPEquivPiPadicInt_mk`, which says the class of a word goes to its exponent-sum vector. In particular xᵢ goes to eᵢ, as the docstring states.

`ℤ_p × ℤ_p` is modelled as `Multiplicative (Fin 2 → ℤ_[p])`. This is the standard way to view an additive group as a multiplicative one, and it is consistent with the rest of the library.

On generality: this is a specific isomorphism tied to one particular presentation, a rank-2 Demushkin normal form with q = 0. The single-relator presentation only makes sense for two generators, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no pro-p presentations, so there is no counterpart there.
